_comment: Reference spacecraft for Phase 9 stage-1 mass closure (V2_BRIEF.md §5).
Interpolating between real spacecraft is defensible; inventing a mass
estimating relationship is not. Stage 2 (component-level MERs) is
EVERY ENTRY IS SECONDARY-SOURCED. These are public spec sheets, mission
portals and encyclopaedia infoboxes, not manufacturer mass budgets. They
are good enough to interpolate between and not good enough to quote to
three figures. Confidence tags say which is which.
_mass_convention: mass_kind distinguishes 'dry' from 'launch'. This matters more than any
other field in the file: a GEO satellite's launch mass is roughly twice
its dry mass (GOES-16: 5192 kg launch, 2857 kg dry), so mixing the two
would corrupt the table beyond use.
Entries whose source gives launch mass and a separate propellant figure
carry mass_kind 'dry' with the arithmetic shown in mass_note.
Entries where only launch mass is published keep mass_kind 'launch' and
are EXCLUDED from dry-mass interpolation by sim/mass_model.py.
_power_convention: power_w is end-of-life or operational average electrical power.
This is the weakest part of the table and the honest place to say so.
Sources report power inconsistently -- beginning-of-life vs end-of-life,
per-panel vs total, array output vs load. Where a source is ambiguous
the entry carries power_confidence 'estimated' and a power_note giving
the raw wording. Expect this to be the dominant error term, ahead of the
_held_out: Three entries carry held_out: true. They are excluded from the table the
interpolator sees and used only to score it (Gate 9).
Selection criteria, fixed BEFORE any prediction was computed:
1. one per size class -- small (140 kg), medium (1016 kg), large (2857 kg)
2. published DRY mass, not launch mass, so the target is unambiguous
3. published power, since that is the predictor
No entry was swapped after seeing a result. V2_BRIEF.md §7: report the
misses, do not tune the table.
_family_note: family exists to prevent leakage. Predicting Sentinel-2 from Sentinel-2B,
or GOES-16 from GOES-17, would be interpolating a satellite from its own
twin and would say nothing about the method. sim/mass_model.py excludes

satellites.name: Dove-3 (Planet Flock)
satellites.mass_note: 3U CubeSat with no propulsion, so launch mass is dry mass.
satellites.power_note: 'approximately 20 watts at maximal power' -- peak, not EOL average.
satellites.solar_array_note: Two 260 x 300 mm deployable wings; body-mounted cells not included.

satellites.name: PROBA-V
satellites.mass_note: Quoted flat as 140 kg; PROBA-V carries no chemical propulsion.
satellites.power_note: 25 solar strings x 12.8 W average EOL per string = 320 W. Computed from the eoPortal EPS description, not quoted directly.
satellites.source: ESA Earth Online, PROBA-V overview; eoPortal PROBA-V

satellites.name: OneWeb
satellites.mass_note: 'a mass of around 150 kg'. Propellant fraction not published.

satellites.name: Starlink v1.5
satellites.mass_note: 227 kg (Baruah et al. 2024) to 303 kg (secondary). See data/satellite_specs.json, which is authoritative for this spacecraft.
satellites.solar_array_note: Derived in Phase 8 from the ~11 m deployed span; see satellite_specs.json v1_5.geometry.

satellites.name: CryoSat-2
satellites.power_note: eoPortal: 'each panel provides power of 850 W at normal solar incidence', two panels in a fixed roof configuration. Both panels are never at normal incidence at once, so total output is below 1700 W and above 850 W. Taken as 850 W; genuinely ambiguous.

satellites.name: KOMPSAT-2 / Arirang-2
satellites.bus_note: Deployed dimensions, not stowed bus envelope.

satellites.name: Sentinel-2
satellites.power_note: Operational power. Arrays give 2300 W BOL / 1730 W EOL.

satellites.name: Himawari-8
satellites.mass_note: Launch mass ~3500 kg; dry 1300 kg. GEO propellant fraction is large.
satellites.source: eoPortal, Himawari-8 and 9; Gunter's Space Page

satellites.name: Sentinel-1
satellites.power_note: Average onboard power at EOL. Arrays give 5900 W EOL.

satellites.name: GOES-16 (GOES-R series)
satellites.mass_note: Launch mass 5192 kg. Dry mass is 55% of launch -- the GEO propellant fraction in one number.
